# Turn sequential ids into random-looking codes

> Scramble turns sequential IDs into random-looking 7-character codes using a keyed Feistel cipher, preventing link enumeration.

_Part of [Creating and resolving share links](share-short-links.md)_

When people create short affiliate links, you want the resulting codes to look random so visitors can't guess other people's links or predict codes in order. Instead of generating and checking random codes until you find one that's free, [`scramble`](share-short-links.md) uses a Feistel network—a mathematical permutation that maps every sequential ID (1, 2, 3, …) to a unique `random-looking` number, then encodes it as a 7-character base62 string. The [`scramble`](share-short-links.md) function does 4 rounds of HMAC-SHA256 mixing using a secret key. Because a Feistel network is a permutation by design, every ID maps to exactly one code and every code maps back to exactly one ID (via [`unscramble`](share-short-links.md)), with no collisions and no uniqueness checks needed. The key ensures different services or instances produce different scrambles from the same IDs. With 40 bits of ID space, you get 1.1 trillion unique codes. When a user creates a link, you lease a sequential ID from [Hand out ids in blocks of 1,000 from Redis](id-lease.md), scramble it with your key to get a number, convert that to base62 via [`toBase62`](share-short-links.md) to get the 7-character code, and store it alongside the link destination in [Creating and resolving share links](share-short-links.md).

**Look at:** [codes.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/domain/codes.ts)

## Pieces

- [Feistel network cipher for sequential IDs](feistel-scramble.md): Scramble and unscramble use a 4-round Feistel network with HMAC-SHA256 to create a bijection from sequential IDs to random-looking numbers and back.
- Base62 encoding for 7-character codes: `ToBase62` converts a number to a base62 string using digits, uppercase and lowercase letters (7 characters by default); [`fromBase62`](share-short-links.md) reverses it.
- Custom alias format validation: [`CUSTOM_ALIAS`](share-short-links.md) regex allows 4–32 character strings starting with alphanumeric, containing only alphanumeric and hyphens.

## Watch out

- The id must fit in 40 bits (0 to 1,099,511,627,775); larger values throw a `RangeError`.
- The scramble key must be consistent to reliably unscramble codes later—a different key will produce garbage.
- Because Feistel networks are permutations, every code is valid and maps to exactly one ID; you do not need a uniqueness check.
- Base62 uses both upper and lowercase letters, so codes are case-sensitive (e.g., 'A' and 'a' are different).
